title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — logicians' definitions mark aptitudo not act (albedo / sight)
pass_a_gloss: Placeus backs the Clavis with the logicians: definition-words often name aptitude, not a completed act—as whiteness is 'color that scatters sight,' meaning born apt to do so.
pass_b_english: In the same sense logicians usually note that words set in definitions mark an aptitude, not an act—as when whiteness is defined as a color that scatters sight, that is, that is born apt to scatter sight.
source_text: Eodem sensu Logici notare solent verba in definitionibus posita aptitudinem, non actum designare, ut cum definitur albedo, Color qui visum disgregat, id est, qui aptus natus est visum disgregare.
